A_general.open_code_note: The public repository is a Claude plugin containing six workflow skills and two commands. Its .mcp.json points to the hosted endpoint, but the repository does not implement that server; its workflow instructions are companion material, not server tool definitions.
A_general.implementation_language: Markdown and JSON for the public Claude plugin; hosted server implementation language NOT FOUND
A_general.license: Apache-2.0 for the public Claude plugin; hosted server license NOT FOUND
other_official_servers: The official Claude plugin is a companion integration that uses the same hosted endpoint and adds skills and commands; it is not documented as a separate MCP server.

B_access_pricing.mcp_access_cost_details: The vendor says the MCP server is included across all Common Room plans, with no separate MCP charge stated. The entry Essential plan is listed at $2,500/month billed annually; Advanced and Enterprise are custom priced.
B_access_pricing.linked_software_cost: Essential: $2,500/month billed annually, five seats included. Advanced and Enterprise: custom pricing.
B_access_pricing.pricing_model_details: Vendor pricing lists plan-level seat, contact, RoomieAI research-credit, and Prospector-credit allowances. The MCP page states inclusion on all plans; no MCP-specific call pricing or limits are published.
B_access_pricing.other_access_restrictions: A Common Room instance and account access are prerequisites. Instance administrators can disable MCP access for the entire instance. Individual OAuth authorization uses the user's permissions and default workspace. Client-side availability may depend on client mode or organization installation.
B_access_pricing.restrictions_controlled_by: Vendor and Common Room instance administrator; user authorizes their own account, while the AI client controls whether and where MCP tools are available.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: Official documentation names five tools: commonroom_get_catalog, commonroom_list_objects, commonroom_create_object, commonroom_update_object, and commonroom_submit_feedback. The endpoint returned HTTP 401 before authentication, so no live tool definitions were obtained.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Docs describe catalog discovery, filtered and paginated object retrieval, object creation and updates, and feedback submission. Exact content block and error formats are not published.
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: OAuth 2.1 per the docs; OAuth-protected endpoint returned HTTP 401 with an unauthorized message. See Authorization entry for metadata.

C_capabilities.description_what_how: The docs list tools but do not document MCP resources. No live authenticated discovery was performed.
The docs show natural-language examples but do not identify MCP prompt objects or describe prompts/list.
The docs say instance administrators can view users who connected an MCP server and the AI assistant used. They do not specify MCP protocol logging or per-tool audit records.
No server-side sampling capability is documented.

C_capabilities.depends_on_mcp_version: OAuth 2.1 is stated by the vendor; MCP protocol version NOT FOUND
C_capabilities.description_what_how: The endpoint returned HTTP 401 and a WWW-Authenticate challenge pointing to https://mcp.commonroom.io/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp. Both protected-resource metadata documents list authorization server https://login.commonroom.io/ and scopes_supported [openid, profile, email, offline_access]. Authorization-server metadata lists registration_endpoint https://login.commonroom.io/oidc/register, PKCE methods [S256, plain], token endpoint https://login.commonroom.io/oauth/token, token auth methods [client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, private_key_jwt, none], and grants [client_credentials, authorization_code, refresh_token, password, implicit, urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code, urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange, http://auth0.com/oauth/grant-type/password-realm, http://auth0.com/oauth/grant-type/passwordless/otp, http://auth0.com/oauth/grant-type/mfa-oob, http://auth0.com/oauth/grant-type/mfa-otp, http://auth0.com/oauth/grant-type/mfa-recovery-code, urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer]. Authorization-server scopes_supported are [openid, profile, offline_access, name, given_name, family_name, nickname, email, email_verified, picture, created_at, identities, phone, address]. Revocation endpoint: https://login.commonroom.io/oauth/revoke. Token lifetime is not stated.
C_capabilities.post_interaction_context_structure: Unauthenticated POST returned {"error":"unauthorized","message":"Authentication required. Reconnect the MCP server to sign in again."}
C_capabilities.authorization_mechanism: OAuth-protected resource metadata and OAuth authorization server metadata; vendor docs specify OAuth 2.1 and individual user authorization. Dynamic Client Registration endpoint is advertised. Metadata lists PKCE S256 and plain. The protected resource advertises openid, profile, email, offline_access; the authorization server advertises the full scopes_supported list given above. Token lifetime is not stated. Revocation endpoint is advertised.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Tools include read operations (catalog and list) and writes (create, update, feedback). Docs describe partial updates and upsert behavior. No tool annotations are published. 2. The server docs recommend asking the AI to summarize bulk writes first; no server-enforced confirmation parameter or workflow is documented. 3. OAuth is per user; docs say existing workspace role-based permissions apply to reads and writes. Instance admins can disable MCP access and view connected users and AI client. Metadata advertises DCR, PKCE S256/plain, token and revocation endpoints; token lifetime and client allowlist are not documented. 4. No read-only endpoint or tool filters are documented. The user’s default workspace is used when multiple workspaces exist; admins can disable MCP for an instance. 5. Docs state users see and modify only data they have permission to access. PII masking or field-specific exclusions are not documented. 6. List supports filtering, sorting, and cursor pagination; no numeric page, time-range, rate, or truncation limits are published. 7. Required fields and supported fields are documented for create/update, but parameter types and unknown-argument handling are not. Contact/organization creation upserts matching records. 8. Admins can view connected users and AI client; MCP call logging, audit records, and telemetry details are not published. 9. commonroom_submit_feedback lets the AI submit feedback on query results to improve response quality; docs say it provides feedback. No upsell or marketing message in tool results is documented. 10. The hosted docs provide behavioral recommendations, including confirmation advice, but do not publish server instructions. The separate public Claude plugin contains six client-side skills. 11. Docs say the AI maintains conversation context; server-side persistent agent memory is not documented. 12. One hosted global endpoint and a flat five-tool list are documented. The Claude plugin uses the endpoint but is not a nested server. 13. No raw API, SQL, or script execution tool is listed.
behavioural_instructions_to_ai_verbatim: These tools are called automatically by the AI based on your natural language requests — you won't need to invoke them by name.

Confirm write operations before chaining them. When asking the AI to create or update many records at once, ask it to summarize what it's about to do before executing, especially for segment changes or custom-field updates.

Mention your role for territory scoping. The MCP server retrieves your user profile automatically, but you can also say "show me accounts in my territory" or "what are my accounts with renewal risk" to scope results to your segments.
D_server_side_logic.server_structure_explanation: The docs describe one hosted endpoint and one flat list of five tools. The separate Claude plugin uses the same endpoint and does not constitute a server hierarchy.

E_aggregated.action_count_comment: The official tool list exists at https://www.commonroom.io/docs/using-common-room/mcp-server/ and names five tools; no separate stated numeric total appears. No catalogue-only tools were added. Claude's connector directory (publisher-verified; listing added February 2026) and MartechDB also report the same five names. MCP.so says its list is unavailable pending authentication; APIs.io and integrations.sh provide no additional verified tool names. The public Claude plugin is a different artifact and its skills are not MCP tools.

actions.description: Discover workspace object types, properties, filters, and sort fields.
Query objects with filtering, cross-object filters, sorting, pagination, or lookup by ID.
Create contacts, organizations, segments, activities, and notes; contacts and organizations upsert matches.
actions.parameters: Object type and fields; Contact requires at least one of email, linkedInUrl, prospectorContactId; Organization requires domain or prospectorCompanyId; Segment requires name; Activity requires contactId, activityType, activityBody; Note requires contactId, note. Optional fields are documented; field data types are not published.

actions.description: Partially update existing contacts and organizations by ID.
actions.parameters: Contact: contactId (required; c_-prefixed), fullName, email, title, companyName, companyDomain, githubUsername, twitterHandle, linkedInUrl, segmentId, customFields. Organization: organizationId (required; o_-prefixed), segmentId, customFields. Field data types are not published.

actions.description: Submit feedback about query results to improve response quality.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The vendor recommends: “Confirm write operations before chaining them. When asking the AI to create or update many records at once, ask it to summarize what it's about to do before executing, especially for segment changes or custom-field updates.” No confirmation enforcement is documented. It also recommends specifying the user's role for territory scoping.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The vendor states: “Write operations respect the same per-user OAuth permissions as read operations.” It says administrators can disable MCP access for an instance and inspect connected users and AI assistants. Pricing page says data is encrypted in transit and at rest and describes controls for access, retention, and deletion. The privacy notice says it does not apply to Customer Data; customer contracts govern processing of that data.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The docs say the server supports reading and writing and that contact and organization creation uses upsert semantics to avoid duplicate records. Pricing says Common Room MCP is included across all plans.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: Per-user access control and upsert behavior are documented features. Admin disabling and connected-user visibility are documented controls. The write-confirmation advice is a text recommendation; enforcement is not documented. Encryption and retention statements are on the pricing page, not tied specifically to MCP request handling.

observations_for_research: The endpoint exposes a feedback-submission tool alongside data retrieval and mutation tools; its published description says it improves response quality.
The vendor recommends confirming bulk writes in natural language but does not publish a server-enforced confirmation mechanism.
OAuth protected-resource scope metadata is broader than the vendor's explanation of per-user product permissions; the metadata does not map individual OAuth scopes to tool operations.
A separate official Claude plugin adds territory scoping, research, prospecting, and meeting-preparation guidance outside the MCP endpoint.
notes: Reviewed links.json, links_check.txt, pages/ and the local GitHub copy. The endpoint returned HTTP 401; OAuth evidence was supplied in the prompt, and no OAuth login or authenticated tool discovery was attempted. The public repository is the vendor's Claude plugin, not server implementation, so it was not used to infer endpoint tools or server capabilities. No official server code, MCP registry entry, numeric tool total, protocol version, tool annotations, schemas for three tools, or initialize instructions were found. Privacy policy was located through official-domain web search. Third-party catalogs were used for comparison only.
